national.title: Congo's Ebola deaths top 5,000 as fear of continent-wide spread mounts
national.summary: Data from the Congolese Ministry of Health showed that the disease has killed 5,026 people out of 10,351 infected, at a nearly 50% lethality rate.
national.body:
Constant Same Bagalwa, Associated Press Constant Same Bagalwa, Associated Press

BUNIA, Congo (AP) — Deaths in Congo's Ebola outbreak have topped 5,000 as the country grapples with the relentless spread of the disease and cases are recorded in other African countries, the latest government data on Saturday shows.

Data from the Congolese Ministry of Health showed that the disease has killed 5,026 people out of 10,351 infected, at a nearly 50% lethality rate. The surge is sparking concerns among experts regarding the authorities' ability to contain the deadly virus.

The latest outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo virus, was declared in mid-May, catching authorities by surprise. They have since struggled to manage it.

It is already the second deadliest Ebola outbreak in history, second only to a two-year-long West Africa outbreak between 2014 and 2016, which killed 11,000 people across multiple countries.

"It is a very tragic milestone because it is just not a number," said Dr. Patrick Otim, a programme area manager with the World Health Organization. "It is families and communities that have been devastated by this outbreak. The number also shows the severity of this outbreak."

2,788 people have recovered from the virus so far. The Bundibugyo virus has no known vaccine or treatment, but health workers treat patients based on symptoms.

Since May, the disease has spread to 67 out of the country's 178 health zones in eight of 26 provinces. Fifty of the affected 67 health zones have active cases.

national.title: More than 5,000 die from Ebola in DR Congo's deadliest outbreak
national.summary: Government data shows that more than 10,000 people have contracted the rare virus.
national.body:
More than 5,000 people have died from an ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, government data shows.

Eight of 26 provinces are now affected, with more than 10,300 confirmed cases.

The outbreak, which started in May, became the country's deadliest in its history in August, public health officials said. The current case fatality rate is 48.6%.

In its latest update, the health ministry said the epicentre of the epidemic remains in the Ituri province, in the north-east of the country, which is a conflict zone, making it harder to contain the virus.

Cases have also been confirmed in Kenya, Nigeria and Uganda.

This marks the 17th outbreak in DR Congo's history, according to the United Nations (UN), and the second largest in history.

The World Health Organization (WHO) office in Africa said a "continued scale-up of key control measures, greater access to affected areas, and community outreach" is needed to end the outbreak.

Testing and treatment is under way, along with clinical trials of vaccines, it added.

national.body: Iran's strikes on more than two dozen U.S. bases in the Middle East focused on early warning systems before hitting aircraft and buildings, causing billions of dollars in equipment damage, according to an Associated Press analysis . The AP independently verified damage to American targets using satellite imagery from multiple providers and spoke to four regional officials who were briefed or have firsthand knowledge of what was hit. The AP found that, through August, more than 115 drone or missile strikes claimed by Iran or Iranian-backed militias damaged or destroyed structures on 26 military bases and other sites with U.S. equipment. The AP found that Iran initially focused its attacks on aircraft hangars and systems that detect incoming strikes, clearing the way for further strikes on warehouses, troop housing and more. The damage has significantly reshaped the American foothold in the Middle East, with two regional officials saying the U.S. has moved many of its assets out of the Persian Gulf. That includes aircraft, air defense systems, communications systems and other equipment crucial to base operations, one of those officials said. Most of the Iranian attacks have been in Kuwait, while U.S. sites in Bahrain, Iraq, Jordan, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates also have been targeted, the analysis of satellite imagery shows. Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait was struck at least 30 times, damaging or destroying at least 15 aircraft hangars, numerous warehouses and 10 buildings near a residential area. Camp Buehring, also in Kuwait, faced even heavier losses. While Iranian attacks made most of its hangars inoperable, gathering places for troops sustained much more damage because the base had limited aircraft. Its gym was destroyed in March and a store for troops to buy products on the base was hit in late July.

national.title: What to know about the $6.3B hack on Binance, likely the biggest-ever crypto theft
national.summary: Here's what we know about the hack, possible North Korean involvement and Binance's investigation.
national.body:
Kaitlyn Huamani, Associated Press Kaitlyn Huamani, Associated Press

Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, said Friday that hackers stole more than $6 billion in what appears to be the largest cryptocurrency heist on record. Blockchain firms have pointed to the attack coming from a North Korean hacking unit.

The company said it has reserved more than $6.34 billion of company funds to cover the stolen assets and was beginning to recover assets for users. Binance worked with blockchain partners to freeze roughly $3 billion in affected assets.

WATCH: $6 billion cryptocurrency heist puts investors on edge

The cryptocurrency exchange has promised to cover all losses, and it has been sharing regular updates on its social media channels as it uncovers more information about the hack.

"We are working nonstop to resolve this," Binance's co-CEO Richard Teng said Friday in a video posted to X.

In an exchange Friday with reporters at the White House, President Donald Trump said U.S. officials were investigating the Binance hack. Asked whether North Korea was involved, Trump said: "We're looking at that."

national.title: G20 foreign ministers in Atlanta meeting head to an ending without consensus on key issues
national.summary: The group will not release a joint communique but will rather rely on a chairman's statement summarizing the talks, which Secretary of State Marco Rubio will release at the conclusion.
national.body:
ATLANTA (AP) — Top diplomats from the Group of 20 largest world economies are wrapping up two days of talks Saturday without reaching consensus on several critical global security issues after divisions, notably over Russia's war with Ukraine, overshadowed the start of the Atlanta meeting.

As a result, the group will not release a joint communique but will rather rely on a chairman's statement summarizing the talks, which Secretary of State Marco Rubio will release at the conclusion, according to diplomats who attended.

WATCH: Rubio welcomes G20 foreign ministers to Atlanta at 'critical moment'

Nonetheless, Rubio said the first day of the session was "very productive" and he was hosting talks with his counterparts from Australia, India and Japan on Saturday before leading the final G20 event. That discussion on supply chains will examine freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz and the Red, Black and South China seas.

"Together, I think that we are mapping a vibrant, dynamic, and bold economic future, one that will pioneer new horizons for the entire world," Rubio said at a reception for participants late Friday.

Rubio had opened the talks Friday with an appeal for unity, but then canceled the traditional group photo of the foreign ministers. European diplomats objected to the inclusion of Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov and threatened to boycott or walk out of the snapshot.

Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski, who was representing his country for the first time as a guest at a G20 meeting, said he was not surprised by the failure to reach consensus.

"We have wars going on, and we have participants in those wars around the table, so it's very difficult to agree on a common line," he told reporters.

national.title: Evacuees from Russia-occupied city where residents ate weeds arrive in Ukraine
national.summary: Residents left the devastated city on Friday following a ceasefire brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump.
national.body:
People evacuated from the devastated Russian-occupied city of Oleshky have crossed into the Ukrainian region of Chernihiv, President Volodymyr Zelensky has confirmed.

There were emotional scenes as some of the residents of the frontline city met relatives they had not seen for years.

Some elderly residents were so weak that they were carried on stretchers. They had been trapped without food, water and electricity, with many resorting to cooking garden weeds to survive.

The Ukrainian president thanked US First Lady Melania Trump for her efforts in brokering a local ceasefire that paved the way for their evacuation on Friday.

"As of now, Ukrainian citizens from Oleshky have crossed the Ukrainian border in the Chernihiv region," Zelensky said in a post on X.

"All of them will receive the assistance they need. It is important that government agencies and all the regional and local authorities involved work effectively and help our people adapt."

The evacuees were taken via Russia and Belarus before being driven across Ukraine's northern border on Saturday.

The oldest evacuee was 94 years old, while the youngest was one, according to Dmytro Lubinets, Ukraine's human rights ombudsman.

national.title: Residents evacuated from Russian-occupied Oleshky reach Ukraine after localized ceasefire
national.summary: The civilians traveled by bus and plane through Russia and Belarus, following a deal brokered by U.S. first lady Melania Trump.
national.body:
Derek Gatopoulos, Associated Press Derek Gatopoulos, Associated Press

CHERNIHIV REGION, Ukraine (AP) — Evacuees from Russian-occupied Oleshky crossed into Ukrainian-held territory Saturday in a major rescue operation carried out under the most significant truce since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine 4½ years ago.

The civilians traveled by bus and plane through Russia and Belarus, following a deal brokered by U.S. first lady Melania Trump. Ukrainian authorities imposed restrictions on disclosing the number of evacuees or the border crossing location. The measures are to safeguard those who chose to remain in Oleshky as well as to protect future humanitarian missions, the organizers said.

The ceasefire in Ukraine's southern Kherson region, which began at 3 a.m. Tuesday, is expected to continue through Sunday evening. The estimated 2,000 remaining residents of Oleshky were offered the choice of traveling to Ukrainian- or Russian-held territory, or remaining in the city with replenished food and medical supplies.

Those who chose to return to Ukraine were taken to the Russian city of Anapa then flown to Homel in Belarus, from where they proceeded back home.

Relatives waited on Saturday at the Ukrainian-Belarusian border, along with aid tents, coffee stands and even provisions to feed the pets the evacuees were bringing with them. Volunteers from organizations, including the Red Cross, Doctors without Borders and the World Central Kitchen, were also there.

Liza Paliy, 19, who last saw her father over 2½ years ago when she, her mother and sister fled from the occupied territory while he stayed behind, was among those waiting.

"We thought at that time that it would be a month, two maximum, and we would return, but unfortunately, two years have already passed," she said.

national.title: Ethiopian PM puts ministers through military training
national.summary: The prime minister has previously emphasised military preparedness as central to his government's ambitions.
national.body:
Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has put his cabinet ministers and other senior government officials through military training, saying armed forces discipline can help build stronger leaders and advance the country's development.

The move is unusual in Ethiopia, where senior civilian government officials are rarely seen undergoing military training.

Those taking part include Speaker of the House of Federation Muferiat Kamil, Finance Minister Fitsum Assefa and Health Minister Mekdes Daba.

It is unclear when the training began or how long it is expected to last.

In his post, the prime minister, who is known as Abiy, said Ethiopia's ambition to achieve universal prosperity required its leadership to be physically fit, morally strong and intellectually capable.

He said military institutions offered valuable lessons in discipline, patriotism, teamwork, accountability and leadership.

"Soldiers have targets while civilians have goals. The objective of both is victory," he said, adding that combining military and civilian disciplines would help create a generation capable of achieving both.

Abiy argued that military training could help develop leaders with a strong sense of purpose, responsibility and the ability to work together towards common objectives.

national.title: Justice Department seeks to isolate Alaska ballots amid criminal probe over Senate candidate
national.summary: The latest developments come amid allegations, first reported by The New York Times, that Democrats recruited a spoiler candidate in the toss-up U.S. Senate race.
national.body:
Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola speaks during a campaign event Thursday, Oct. 29, 2026, in Juneau, Alaska. Chloe Anderson/AP hide caption

ANCHORAGE, Alaska — The U.S. Department of Justice pushed Friday for a court order to isolate certain Alaska ballots to investigate potential voter confusion, while federal officials confirmed the existence of a criminal probe over a Senate candidate who shares a name with the Republican incumbent.

Elections Alaska's all-important Senate race is roiled by a report on alleged spoiler candidate The dueling developments came days before Tuesday's ranked choice general election, in a race headlined by two-term Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan and Democratic former U.S. Rep. Mary Peltola. The race is among a handful nationwide expected to determine control of the Senate.

Alaska U.S. Attorney Michael Heyman told reporters in Anchorage that the investigation has been ongoing for several months, but recent revelations from The New York Times that Peltola's campaign appeared to be involved in recruiting retired teacher Dan J. Sullivan have resulted in a "significant surge of law enforcement assets to Alaska."

Separately, the Justice Department — as part of a lawsuit it filed last week — asked a judge to order that state elections officials isolate ballots ranking Dan J. Sullivan to investigate potential voter "confusion" with the senator. The owner of a boat dealership in the candidate's hometown of Petersburg who had donated to his campaign told The Associated Press that an FBI agent visited the business and wanted to know whether he had been misled by Dan J. Sullivan's candidacy. He said he had not and that "Everybody knows who the incumbent is."

Alaska Assistant U.S. Attorney E. Bryan Wilson, in a filing, said the government "seeks to preserve and segregate all ballots ranking Daniel J. Sullivan for the purposes of investigating whether such ranking was the product of voter confusion, should such an investigation become necessary."

The Department of Justice also filed with the court a list of proposed questions it seeks to compel the Peltola campaign and the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee to answer as part of the civil case seeking to block certification of the Senate race if the incumbent loses. President Donald Trump has said he told the department to file the case.

Alaska U.S. Attorney Michael Heyman told reporters in Anchorage that the investigation has been ongoing for several months, but recent revelations from The New York Times that Peltola's campaign appeared to be involved in recruiting retired teacher Dan J. Sullivan have resulted in a "significant surge of law enforcement assets to Alaska."

Separately, the Justice Department — as part of a lawsuit it filed last week — asked a judge to order that state elections officials isolate ballots ranking Dan J. Sullivan to investigate potential voter "confusion" with the senator. The owner of a boat dealership in the candidate's hometown of Petersburg who had donated to his campaign told The Associated Press that an FBI agent visited the business and wanted to know whether he had been misled by Dan J. Sullivan's candidacy. He said he had not and that "Everybody knows who the incumbent is."

Alaska Assistant U.S. Attorney E. Bryan Wilson, in a filing, said the government "seeks to preserve and segregate all ballots ranking Daniel J. Sullivan for the purposes of investigating whether such ranking was the product of voter confusion, should such an investigation become necessary."

national.body: DeMonica Amerson's diagnosis of multiple sclerosis in 2001 had been a shock. No one in her family had ever had the autoimmune condition, and it had been difficult to diagnose. Doctors had first thought she had optic neuritis because her symptoms were in her eyes. Then they suspected lupus. After a spinal tap, she was diagnosed with MS. At the time, Amerson had never heard about the condition. She had just graduated from college and expected to be in the prime of her life. Instead, she had to give herself daily shots to treat the condition. "I was mad, I was hurt, I was nervous, confused, all the things," said Amerson. But over the years, her perspective changed. As MS treatment evolved, she moved from daily shots to a monthly infusion. A port was placed in her chest to make the medication easier to deliver. She engaged in advocacy and fundraising through the MS National Foundation. She got married and welcomed two daughters, and worked as a school administrator. Even as her condition threw curveballs, including the occasional relapse, she "just kept going." Amerson attributed those relapses to the progressive nature of MS. Her doctors never suggested otherwise. Then, in 2019, she had a significant flare. She was lethargic, and her legs were numb. Amerson immediately went to the hospital, missing her daughter's birthday party. In the ER, she began to feel pressure in her eyes and began vomiting. An on-call neurologist examined her and ran a specialized blood test. Eventually, Amerson's condition stabilized, and she was discharged. A few days after returning home, she received a call from the neurologist. The doctor believed she had a rare autoimmune disorder and recommended she see her neurologist. Amerson was horrified to receive that diagnosis on top of her MS. When she saw her neurologist, he sent her to a specialist. Follow-up testing by the specialist revealed something shocking: Amerson had never had multiple sclerosis at all. national.title: Drone photo award winners: Far-out landscapes. Ship recycling. Rugs, rugs rugs!
national.summary: The Siena Drone Photo Awards for 2026 offer breathtaking bird's-eye views of our planet, revealing landscapes, livelihoods and human stories often invisible from the ground.
national.body:
It's a mega-recycling effort: A crew of 60 men use blow torches and winches to break down a ship that had carried liquid natural gas. Tons of metal parts will be harvested to resell overseas. This photo by George Steinmetz, from the Bay of Bengal in Bangladesh, is the overall winner in the 2026 Siena Drone Photo Awards contest. George Steinmetz hide caption

It looks like a spacecraft that settled gently onto a golden beach.

Off the coast of Bangladesh, an enormous vessel lies stranded on the mudflats, its steel hull partially dismantled as workers mill around it. This unusual aerial view of a tanker, specially designed to transport liquified natural gas used for cooking, electricity and transport, won photographer George Steinmetz the top prize — overall winner of the 2026 Siena Drone Photo Awards.

Each year, the Siena Drone Photo Awards highlight bird's-eye views of our planet, revealing landscapes, livelihoods and human stories often invisible from the ground. Here, we've selected some of this year's winning and highly commended photographs, focusing on the countries of the Global South.

In an interview with NPR, Steinmetz says he's been long fascinated by Bangladesh's shipbreaking industry, where enormous vessels from around the globe, nearing the end of their working lives, are dismantled and their materials recovered for reuse. The photograph is titled "Shipbreaking on the mudflats, Bay of Bengal." Steinmetz sent up his drone north of Chattogram (Chittagong), along this 13-mile coastal strip, offering a stark glimpse into what this industry is like.

He was exploring the relationship between human populations and the environment for a book project and saw the industry as an extraordinary example of recycling on a vast scale.

Undeterred, he surveyed and photographed the entire coastline north of Chattogram with his drone, searching for a vessel that would make an especially striking photograph. He eventually settled on the liquid natural gas tanker. "The trick for me was to find the right ship, that was in a really interesting state of disassembly. And these tankers are very unusual boats. It just looked weird, like some kind of a spaceship. It takes workers a long time to break it down. And then they have to wait for the tide to be right so they can pull the pieces ashore. They have big winches and boats that they use to get the stuff ashore."

He was able to convince the owner of the tanker to allow him to photograph it. The timing of the drone photo was crucial. Steinmetz wanted to capture the vessel at low tide, when the surrounding mudflats were exposed and workers could be seen moving around its enormous hull. Their tiny figures would look like ants, giving viewers a sense of the ship's mammoth scale. He spent several days photographing the vessel, returning as the tides shifted and the workers continued to take the ship apart for scrap metal.

national.body: Petersburg, Alaska — Daniel J. Sullivan, the independent candidate running for Senate in Alaska whose name is almost identical to the Republican senator running for reelection, left his hometown of Petersburg earlier this week, multiple sources confirmed to CBS News.One resident and former student of Sullivan's said she saw Sullivan on a flight to Anchorage on Monday — two days before The New York Times first reported that he was recruited by operatives linked to Democrat Mary Peltola's campaign. The source added she did not know where Sullivan was headed, but another friend said he and his wife are known among friends as "world travelers." Sullivan's current whereabouts after leaving his hometown are not clear.Dozens of Petersburg residents also told CBS News they never saw or received any campaign materials like mailers, flyers, brochures or signs since the former elementary school teacher announced his candidacy last spring."I don't think it's a serious candidacy," said Andrew Worhatch, a Petersburg fisherman. "I haven't seen a platform."Just days before the midterm elections, a CBS News crew on the ground in Petersburg likewise found no indication of any active campaigning by the candidate, including outside his own home, which sits adjacent to the main coastal highway.Still, Sullivan has his supporters — and voters — including Keely Hankins, who said she thinks "Petersburg Dan" is the only candidate capable of representing Southeast Alaska."I've known Dan for a long time. I know his family. I know he's raised good children, and he's always been a really great role model for his students," Hankins maintained. "If you intend to vote and intentionally vote, you know who you're going to vote for, and it says 'Daniel J. Sullivan, Jr.,' then it says 'Dan Sullivan, incumbent.' Just read the paper. local.body: Two pets are dead Friday night following a high-rise fire in Lockport.According to the City of Lockport Fire Department, just before 8:30 p.m., Lockport Fire Department responded to reports of smoke coming from a third floor apartment building on 77 Main Street.Crews found smoke visible from the exterior window but found no visible fire venting from the building. Crews determined the fire was on the fourth floor of the apartment building.LFD say there was no active fire observed but remnants of a large lithium-ion battery was smoldering in the corner of the living room.The fire was declared out within 10 minutes after arriving to the scene and crews worked on the scene for 1.5 hours. Three people suffered from non-life threatening smoke inhalation while attempting to rescue pets within the apartment. Two were taken to Lockport Hospital and one was taken to ECMC as a precaution.According to the LFD, the tenant was home at the time of the fire and attempted to rescue the animals but was overcome by smoke. Two pets were found deceased and one pet was successfully removed.The fire was caused by a lithium-ion battery, which was used to power an e-bike device.The estimated property damage was $15,000.

local.body:
A boil order has been lifted for village of Fredonia users, but conservation of water is still being urged.

On Saturday morning, the Chautauqua County Health Department said two consecutive days of testing indicate that the water in the distribution system is safe for drinking, cooking, making ice, brushing teeth and making coffee. The filtration equipment at the water treatment plant is still under stress due to the high levels of organic material in the raw Fredonia Reservoir water.

In recent days, the water treatment plant has been able to produce water that has consistently met New York state Department of Health safety standards. In order to continue making safe water, the filters will need to maintain a steady backwashing schedule which means more of the clean water that is produced at the plant will need to be used by the plant.

In order to support the need for frequent filter backwashes residents, businesses, and institutions must continue efforts to conserve water.

The village of Fredonia will continue to monitor the situation and provide updates as needed. “Community cooperation is essential to ensuring the continued availability of safe drinking water for all,” a statement from the county noted.

He tells me the construction has been a nuisance, but amidst the challenges he's decided to open a new restaurant at the former Vasilis location, next door to his current business.He's in the middle of renovating the space to become Sam's Benedict, a restaurant operated by his wife, Sam."The entire place is getting an overhaul, table chairs furniture, menu," Flanagan said.The business owner plans for the restaurant to be open for breakfast, lunch and dinner. He told me he's able to expand due to his wife's online catering business."Her reach has pulled the people in, and now our business is at capacity," Flanagan said.WATCH: Buffalo business owner expands with new restaurant despite ongoing Main Street construction woesFlanagan admitted he has some concerns about the length of the construction project but overall he's optimistic."I have high hopes for downtown. It's been dead since they first did this in the '70s when they put the rail in. Hopefully this fixes that mistake," Flanagan said. "Hopefully I can set an example for other businesses to come down here and be successful."Flanagan plans to open the new restaurant in January.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. local.body:
CASSADAGA — An early morning one-vehicle accident has led to the death of a teenager and has a community in mourning.

Chautauqua County sheriff’s deputies report at 12:37 a.m. Saturday, they responded with New York State Police, Cassadaga and Stockton Fire Departments to the accident on Maple Avenue. As a result of the accident, one male juvenile sustained serious injuries and was flown to an area hospital for treatment. A second male juvenile sustained fatal injuries and was pronounced deceased.

Both involved in the accident were Cassadaga Valley Central School students. In a Facebook post, the district called the news “heartbreaking” and noted it will have counseling available today and Sunday.

“Our hearts are with both families as they navigate this unimaginable tragedy,” the post said. “We ask that our community respect the privacy of both families during this incredibly difficult time.

“We know this news will deeply affect our students, our staff, and our entire community. Please know that our crisis response team is mobilizing to provide support to students and staff. “We will open the crisis center today at 2 p.m. at the middle high school and (Sunday) at noon. Please enter through the main doors under the clock tower.

“If you need support, connect with those close to you or our team. There are no perfect words for a moment like this. Today, we simply need to take care of one another, give our students grace, and remember that we are one school community, and we will continue to support one another as we navigate this heartbreaking tragedy.”

The accident remains under investigation by the Chautauqua County Sheriff’s Office. Additional information will be released as it becomes available.

local.title: Domestic violence case handling changes in imperfect system
local.summary: More often than not, when it comes to domestic violence cases in court, victims find it hard to navigate the system or to get themselves heard. Attorney Sally Jaroszynski has been practicing law for over 30 years, and in that time she said things have changed when it comes to domestic violence cases
local.body:
More often than not, when it comes to domestic violence cases in court, victims find it hard to navigate the system or to get themselves heard.

Attorney Sally Jaroszynski has been practicing law for over 30 years, and in that time she said things have changed when it comes to domestic violence cases, and while things remain difficult to navigate there is also help for victims out there.

The way cases were handled in 1993, Jaroszynski said, when she first began versus how domestic violence cases are handled now is very different.

"I think the courts have made some strides in how they handle domestic violence cases, but it's tricky and difficult to navigate sometimes," Jaroszynski said. "When I started practicing in '93 we didn't have an Integrated Domestic Violence Court."

Something else that is different these days, Jaroszynski said, is that there is the ability with the IDV Court for one judge to hear multiple different aspects or proceedings in connection to the case, as that judge presides over all of them, even with them being separate proceedings. Chautauqua County has that in IDV court with Judge Stephen Cass, who Jaroszynski said does a wonderful job as he is very well trained in domestic violence. But, she added, if a case does not get pulled into IDV court, that is when people can get lost and struggles can begin.

"It's hard when you're not trained in domestic violence as extensively as maybe our IDV judges are, because I think the difficulty is that people believe just a couple of incidents of physical violence is what is considered domestic violence," Jaroszynski said. "Domestic violence is so much more difficult to prove than sometimes physical violence."

Other areas of domestic violence that Jaroszynski said are more difficult to prove include coercive control, or restricting a partner's freedom or activities. Other forms of abuse take the forms of psychological abuse, economic abuse, stalking or harassment, and one that Jaroszynski said they see even more often today, and never saw when she first started, is through technology and social media.

"All of those issues together are things that pop up in domestic violence that I've had several clients who I sit with and counsel for the first time, and they have no idea that the technology abuse and the stalking and harassment and the economic and psychological abuse and coercive control, they don't even recognize that that's domestic violence," Jaroszynski said. "If they don't recognize it, you better hope that the judge does. And sometimes, it's really hard to prove."

local.body:
The family of a Jamestown man killed in a wrong-way crash in 2023 on Interstate 86 is refiling its case in state Supreme Court after the original 2025 filing was dismissed due to a procedural error.

Sandra Town, Joseph Town and the estate of Todd A. Town refiled their suit in state Supreme Court earlier this week after the 2025 case was dismissed because of an issue with the way the lawsuit was served upon Werner Enterprises Inc. and Brandon D. Cox. The lawsuit seeks compensatory damages for the wrongful death of Todd A. Town, compensatory damages for injuries and losses sustained by Sandra Town and Todd Town before he died, funeral expenses, damages arising from pre-impact physical pain and suffering, mental terror and mental anguish of the Towns.

A lawsuit filed in 2025 was dismissed on May 6 by state Supreme Court Justice Grace Hanlon, who granted a motion to dismiss because the lawsuit had not been properly filed upon Werner and Cox.

State law allows plaintiffs to file a new action in certain circumstances within six months of a similar filing being dismissed. That time period ends on Nov. 5, 2026, attorney Andrew Debbins wrote in his affirmation in support of an Order to Show Cause filed this week in state Supreme Court in Mayville. Debbins is asking the court to allow the filing to be served upon Joel B. Schechter, a Buffalo attorney who represented Werner Enterprises in the original lawsuit. Personally serving Cox would be difficult in nine days since the truck driver is often

"The plaintiffs respectfully ask that this court order that service upon Mr. Schechter, including by email, be deemed good and sufficient service upon the defendants," Debbins wrote. "Service by other means within the required timeframe is impracticable."

The accident happened Jan. 28, 2023, when two people, one of whom was driving the wrong way in the westbound lane of Interstate 86 between the Strunk Road and North Main Street Extension exits.

According to the New York State Police, the agency handling the investigation, a driver in a 2009 Toyota Camry traveling east struck a westbound 2019 Ram 1500. The Ram was then hit from behind by a 2020 Freightliner.

The operator of the vehicle traveling in the wrong direction, later identified as Mathew A. Berry of Randolph, was pronounced dead at the scene. Police said Berry had been reported missing earlier in the day. There were two occupants in the Ram that was traveling west; one of the occupants, identified as Jamestown resident Todd A. local.summary: MILWAUKEE — It was only fitting that the Milwaukee Brewers celebrated their first World Series title with a beer-soaked celebration worthy of their name. “We’ve had way too many parade beers,” team captain and designated hitter Christian Yelich said Friday at a rally that capped a daylong party with
local.body:
MILWAUKEE -- It was only fitting that the Milwaukee Brewers celebrated their first World Series title with a beer-soaked celebration worthy of their name.

“We’ve had way too many parade beers,” team captain and designated hitter Christian Yelich said Friday at a rally that capped a daylong party with fans. “I took the trophy to the face, got a black eye. It’s all worth it. It’s for you guys. We should celebrate forever.”

The small-market Brewers gave their long-suffering fans the championship they had been waiting for with a 4-1 win over the Tampa Bay Rays on Wednesday, clinching the Series in five games. It was their first time playing in the Fall Classic in 44 years.

“Unbelievable,” said parade attendee Mark Diedrich, a 76-year-old from who has been an on-and-off partial season ticket holder since the 1980s. “You just never thought it would happen. But it did.”

Before the rally at American Family Insurance Amphitheater near the shore of Lake Michigan, the Brewers held a parade through downtown Milwaukee. Exuberant fans flooded the streets, watched from parking garages and cheered from office building windows.

Milwaukee police estimated that over 750,000 attended the parade or rally, well above their initial expectations of about 400,000.

“That was incredible -- incredible,” manager Pat Murphy said. “I kept thinking I saw the same people over and over, and we were just going in a circle. There’s no way there’s that many people who live here.”

Then came a rally that featured World Series MVP William Contreras joining in on the fans’ “MVP” chants.

local.summary: Neighbors near the Buffalo River are raising questions about a mysterious oily, rainbow-colored sheen after crews removed booms that had been placed in the water in early October.
local.body: Neighbors near the Buffalo River are raising questions about a mysterious oily, rainbow-colored sheen after crews removed booms that had been placed in the water in early October. One kayaker said she may have spotted signs of the problem months ago.Jaime Hodge said she and her family were kayaking on the Buffalo River over Memorial Day weekend when they came around a bend near the foot of Pomona Place and noticed a substance in the water, along with a strong odor."The smell of gas is horrible," Hodge said in video taken during the kayaking trip.Hodge said a friend reported what they saw to the state Department of Environmental Conservation, and DEC trucks arrived on Bailey Avenue shortly afterward. She said she never heard what investigators determined.She thinks it's possible that the spill she saw is the one that has caused new oil sheens along the Buffalo River this fall."Since this was May and we're now, you know, two days away from November, I would think in that time they could have at least found where it's coming from," Hodge said.The discovery has taken on new significance as questions continue about the oily sheen seen elsewhere on the Buffalo River.On Friday morning, a crew contracted by the DEC was seen removing booms from the river near the South Ogden Street Bridge, even as the oily sheen remained visible in the water.Two South Ogden Street residents expressed concern about removing the booms before the source of the sheen has been identified."We have no definitive answer from the DEC about what's in the river," one resident, identified as Andrew, said. "We have no definitive answer of where it's coming from, and the one thing that they were able to do is control it. local.title: Outcome of the Fairport mayoral election could take time
local.summary: How close the vote is likely will determine the level of priority given to sorting through write-ins.
local.body:
Voters in Fairport might have to wait some time before they know the outcome of the mayoral race there.

That's because while Deputy Mayor Heidi Woika is the only name on the ballot in Tuesday's general election , Village Trustee Tracy Briggs has mounted a formidable write-in campaign after narrowly losing the Democratic primary.

Election Night results will include vote tallies for Woika and a general category for write-ins, which could be Briggs or any name a voter chooses. Those will be reviewed after the election by a bipartisan team that will tabulate totals and assess how to count write-in votes with misspellings or partial names.

How close the two vote tallies are likely will determine the level of priority given to sorting through those write-ins to determine — in a matter of days, or weeks — how many get counted for Briggs.

entertainment.title: Macklemore Wraps Up Free Palestine Tour in London: “It Was More Uncomfortable for Me to Stay Silent”
entertainment.summary: The concerts, raising money for Palestinian causes, come weeks after Macklemore was controversially dropped from Ed Sheeran's Loop Tour.
entertainment.body:
Macklemore brought the final night of his Free Palestine Tour to London on Friday, telling a U.K. audience: “I don’t believe that staying silent is brave.”

The sold-out event at the capital’s OVO Arena Wembley boasted a crowd of over 12,500 people, who cheered and screamed as the U.S. rapper spoke.

The gigs come weeks after he was removed from Ed Sheeran’s Loop Tour for expressing his pro-Palestine views on stage. Sheeran later said it was a promoter decision to drop Macklemore, and that venues set to host the concerts threatened to pull out if Macklemore was on the bill. Related Stories Movies 'Fuxi: Four Tales of Feasting' Review: Whimsical Chinese Film Explores Myth and History Through a Series of Tasty Treats Business Japan's Anime Industry Hits a Record High of $28 Billion in 2025

In response, Macklemore launched his own benefit concert with acts in the British capital such as Aja Monet, Cure for Paranoia, Dana Saleh, Nemahsis, Lucas Jones, Paloma Faith, Roze, Shadia Mansour and Vic Mensa. Swedish climate activist Greta Thunberg was among the guest speakers, along with Hollywood superstars Mark Ruffalo, Susan Sarandon, Javier Bardem, Cynthia Nixon, as well as Melissa Barrera and Julian Casablancas, dialing in remotely.

“It was more uncomfortable for me to stay silent than to say something,” said Macklemore about the situation with Sheeran. “And I just want to say, I don’t believe that saying something is brave. I don’t believe that saying something is courageous. I believe that saying something is human. And those children in Gaza are our children. There is no separation.”

He continued: “I want to say thank you to every single soul that is in here tonight who decided to step up, leave their couch, be in community, be reminded and feel what that frequency of love feels like.” Macklemore added about the 50 members of the British House of Lords who urged the U.K. government to ban his concert: “Regardless of what the 50 Lords have to say, this is a story of equality for all human beings around this earth.”

All proceeds from the concerts in Dublin, Paris and London will go toward organizations supporting Palestinian communities through humanitarian relief, medical care, education, advocacy, policy change and community initiatives, according to the rapper’s team. entertainment.body:
Harry Styles went back to where it all started for Harryween.

At Madison Square Garden on Friday (Oct. 30), the 29th night of his 30-show Together, Together residency, Styles changed into the outfit he wore for his 2010 X Factor audition and performed Stevie Wonder ’s “Isn’t She Lovely,” the song that got him through to the next round at 16. He even repeated a line from that day, telling the crowd, “I work in a bakery,” a nod to the part-time job he held in his Cheshire hometown of Holmes Chapel.

The audition outfit was a mid-show swap. Styles opened the night dressed as Elvis Presley , while his band and dancers came as different versions of Styles from across his career. The Elvis nod tracks: the first song Styles ever recorded was a cover of Presley’s “The Girl of My Best Friend.” Related Morgan Wallen 'Now' Has Another Record on Billboard's Country Airplay Chart Aaron Frazer Doubles Down on Soul with New 'Corners' EP: 'Simple Things Can Be Elegant' Mizuho Kusanagi's 'Akatsuki no Yona' Vol. 48 Debuts at No. 1 on Billboard Japan Book Hot 100 Explore Harry Styles One Direction Stevie Wonder See latest videos, charts and news

Footage released by the show in 2022 revealed he opened with Train ’s “Hey, Soul Sister,” and only sang the Wonder song a cappella after Simon Cowell asked to hear him without a backing track. He was later placed in One Direction alongside Niall Horan , Louis Tomlinson , Zayn Malik and the late Liam Payne . Earlier this month, Styles debuted “What Is Enough,” a song written for Payne, at the same venue on the second anniversary of Payne’s death.

Costumed covers have become a Harryween tradition. At the first edition, at MSG in 2021, Styles dressed as Dorothy to sing “Over the Rainbow,” then came out as a clown the next night to cover Britney Spears ’ “Toxic.” In 2022, at Los Angeles’ Kia Forum, he dressed as Grease ’s Danny Zuko for “Hopelessly Devoted to You.”

Tame Impala have just come off their biggest Australian tour to date, and their album Deadbeat leads next month’s ARIA Awards with eight nominations, tied with Genesis Owusu.

Tame Impala recently wrapped the Australian leg of their Deadbeat Tour, which featured multiple arena shows in Brisbane, Melbourne and Sydney before finishing with two hometown performances in Perth on Oct. 24 and 25. Parker and his band are set to return to the road in May 2027 for a string of UK and European arena dates, followed by several summer festival appearances.

Seal’s original topped the Billboard Hot 100 for a week in August 1995 after its Batman Forever placement and won three Grammys the following year, including record and song of the year.

entertainment.body:
The 2026 Daytime Emmy Awards were presented Friday night, with General Hospital taking home the top prize of best daytime drama.

The series, which went into Friday night’s show up for 13 awards, won three other awards and saw its Genie Francis receive the lifetime achievement award. Beyond the Gates also won four awards, with star Tamara Tunie winning best actress in a daytime drama series. Best actor in a daytime drama went to The Bold and the Beautiful ‘s Scott Clifton.

Tunie, who won her first Daytime Emmy, paid tribute to the “host of Black actresses who paved the way for me, and I feel them as I stand here tonight, beginning with the legendary Cicely Tyson, the first Black woman to appear on a daytime television show, The Guiding Light .” Related Stories TV The Hollywood Reporter Wins 2026 Daytime Emmy Award Music Tom Morello, Annie Lennox, 'KPop Demon Hunters' Songwriters Honored at 2026 SONA Awards

Fellow best actress nominee Heather Tom, from The Bold and the Beautiful , was eyeing a record-setting seventh trophy, which would have made her the most awarded actress in daytime history.

The Young and the Restless led this year’s nominees with 18 nominations. Though it only won three awards, two of those came in the supporting performer categories. Roger Howarth was named best supporting actor, and Beth Maitland was named best supporting actress.

The Kelly Clarkson Show won five awards, including best daytime talk series, but the singer-host of the now-completed talk show didn’t appear to be at the Daytime Emmys . And Clarkson didn’t win the award for best daytime talk series host. Instead that honor went to fellow former talk show host Sherri Shepherd, whose eponymous talk show was canceled after four seasons.

Other notable winners include Tracee Ellis Ross, who won best travel and adventure program for her Solo Traveling show; Keke Palmer, who won for her work executive producing Glam Through the Ages ; and Ina Garten, who won best culinary host for her Be My Guest Food Network series, which was named best culinary instructional series.

Midway through the ceremony, NATAS chair Terry O’Reilly offered a timely, political speech, just days ahead of the 2026 midterm elections. Speaking about a congressman who was jailed in 1798 after criticizing the president in print, O’Reilly highlighed the power of the people.

entertainment.summary: The president slammed the TV host in a Sunday post, writing that he is a "COMPLETE AND TOTAL LOSER."
entertainment.body:
Logo text Bill Maher has responded to President Donald Trump ‘s lengthy social media post where he slammed him as a “complete and total loser,” and shared more details about their recent dinner at the White House.

During Friday’s episode of Real Time with Bill Maher , the comedian addressed a few of the statements made in Trump’s post. He began the monologue by discussing the upcoming midterms and how former President Barack Obama caused a “big scandal” for a comment he made at a campaign rally saying that Trump has “got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory.” Related Stories Music Canadian Rock Icon Bryan Adams Takes Aim at Trump, Says His Protest Song Gets Standing Ovations in Red States (Exclusive) Music Bryan Adams Releases New Trump Protest Song "Lake Ontario"

Maher said, “And the Republicans all said, ‘Leave the Cheesecake Factory out of this!’ Well, I mean, I should know. I just had dinner there. I hear it went well. What have you heard?”

The host then asked, “Now, did you see the 1,300-word Tweet he sent out? Longest ever. Kind of a flex.” He joked that “dining at the White House is the opposite of the Cheesecake Factory. After you leave, they review you.”

“He went off on me like Kelly Clarkson in a toy store,” Maher added. “I mean, eating with Trump is like dating Taylor Swift. It’s a lot of laughs at the time, but later on, they’re tearing you a new asshole.”

Maher was then handed a printed copy of Trump’s Truth Social post, and began to “address a few of the allegations.” Before that, he noted, “Look, I don’t want it to be this way. The whole point of having these dinners was talk, disagree, but listen, which he does in person, but don’t hate each other. And then I go back to my job here and then the heartaches begin.”

“It begins, ‘Let’s talk about the complete and total loser Bill Maher.’ You got me there. I’ll own that,” Maher joked, going on to explain “what pisses me off” is that “he doesn’t even notice what I say,” specifically citing a line in Trump’s post where he wrote, “[Maher] doesn’t think it was a good thing to take the Nuclear Weapon away from Iran, which shows you that he is not very smart.” Real Time then played a series of clips showcasing the opposite of Trump’s claim.

Maher then moved on to another section: “Page two, he talks about how I call him incessantly. I’ve never called you, you call me. I’d be afraid to call you. You’re the president. I think you’re too busy. Well, plainly not. He’s talking about me, ‘He invited himself to the White House.’ As if you could do that. ‘Sir, Bill Maher is here.’ ‘Well, he’s not invited, but the law.”

entertainment.summary: Police arrested Downer's boyfriend, Delorean Bijon Brandon, and Kaylee Nicole Markowski on Thursday.
entertainment.body:
Two people have been arrested for the murder of Christina Downer, the sister to Saturday Night Live writer Jimmy Fowlie, the Los Angeles Police Department announced Friday.

Police arrested Downer’s boyfriend, Delorean Bijon Brandon, and Kaylee Nicole Markowski on Thursday.

“On December 18, 2025, Christina Downer was reported missing after her ex-husband requested a welfare check when he had not heard from her for an extended period of time. Downer’s boyfriend, Delorean Brandon, claimed that she had moved out several months earlier, leaving behind all her belongings, including her vehicle and dog,” the LAPD said. Related Stories Movies 'Fair Play' Doc About Olympic Gymnast Jordan Chiles Set for 2027 Release on Hulu, Disney+ (Exclusive) Movies Bill Hader Is the Cat in the Hat -- This Time a "Much Different Version" Than He Played on 'SNL'

In their statement, police said, “Robbery- Homicide Division detectives assumed the investigation after Downer’s cellphone was discovered washed ashore on Santa Monica Beach. Through various investigative techniques, detectives identified Delorean Brandon and Kaylee Markowski as the individuals responsible for Downer’s murder, the disposal of her body, and the concealment of their involvement.”

On Dec. 22, 2025, Fowlie shared a social media post asking for help finding his missing sister, sharing a multiple of images of Downer. Months later, in April of this year, he announced that “the LAPD has informed our family that Christina is no longer alive, and the case has officially transitioned from a missing person to a homicide investigation.”

The SNL writer shared in his April post that he believes his sister’s “phone and social media were compromised” in the weeks before she went missing, and those who took her phone “used it to hide the fact she was gone, to ask for money, and to create a false narrative that she was going ‘off the grid.’”

“I am sharing this because I believe that whoever is responsible is hoping to erase her in every way possible,” he wrote. “I want to amplify her story in the only way I know how. And to express that she was a beautiful person who matters in this world, especially to me.”

The LAPD’s Robbery-Homicide Division will present the case to the L.A. Country District Attorney’s Office for filing consideration. The investigation is still ongoing.

entertainment.title: ‘Fuxi: Four Tales of Feasting’ Review: Whimsical Chinese Film Explores Myth and History Through a Series of Tasty Treats
entertainment.summary: In Qiu Jiongjiong's latest, highly stylized sets and costumes contribute to a strange banquet of storytelling where food plays a key role.
entertainment.body:
Following up his well-received 2021 feature A New Old Play , Sichuan-reared Chinese writer-director Qiu Jiongjiong continues to deploy heightened artifice and quasi-theatrical mannerisms (painted stage sets, rippling cloths representing water, actors in wacky costumes playing astral bodies or dogs, and so on) with his eccentric but addictive latest, Fuxi: Four Tales of Feasting .

Although Fuxi runs a trim 135 minutes compared to New Old Play ’s three-hour run time, Qiu still manages to cover more than 2,000 years of myth, history and mythic history with a quartet of stories that revolve around special meals and banquets. (The word “fuxi,” intertitles helpfully explain, can either be a noun meaning delicious food or a verb signifying the savoring of such delicacies.) Related Stories Movies Eric Bauza Remembered as a "Once-in-a-Generation" Talent Who Gave Looney Tunes a New Voice Music Canadian Rock Icon Bryan Adams Takes Aim at Trump, Says His Protest Song Gets Standing Ovations in Red States (Exclusive) Fuxi: Four Tales of Feasting The Bottom Line Spicy and addictive, if not easily digestible. Venue: Tokyo Film Festival (Competition) Cast: Lee Kang Sheng, Lee Hong-Chi, Annie Chen, Fan Guang Yao, Wang Talu, Wang Yitong, Xue Xuchun, Wang Hai, Zhou Jiarui Director/screenwriter: Qiu Jiongjiong 2 hours 15 minutes

The different segments, each one offering varying mixtures of slapstick comedy and memento mori solemnity, don’t have much to do with one another story-wise. So Qiu pulls it all together with a framing device about a film crew making each segment, the tales linked by the presence of the sun or Sol (Wen Ke) and Luna aka the moon (Xiao Luxi’); both actors rock massive sun- and moon-shaped headpieces.

Yes, the whole thing is just as bizarre as it sounds, but Qiu’s relentless visual brio keeps the soufflé aloft while the serious intent adds a complex, umami aftertaste with a hint of the tingly, numbing flavor so distinctive in Sichuan cuisine.

Indeed, much of the dialogue here is reportedly in the Sichuan dialect, a nuance that native speakers are likely to appreciate more than the international viewers, who may have caught this at the Tokyo Film Festival, where it premiered in competition. Nevertheless, the performances and the English-language subtitles succeed in getting across the mix of high and low cultures on display here, as each chapter throws together peasants and aristocrats, ordinary folk and fantastic beings, actors and filmmakers in a giddy muddle. The effect is a little reminiscent of commedia dell’arte with all that breaking-of-the-fourth-wall stuff, especially since the mise en scene here is so archly theatrical.

entertainment.title: Inside Jacksonville’s Historic — And Haunted? — Florida Theatre, Which Turns 100 Next Year
entertainment.summary: The nearly century-old venue has hosted acts including Elvis Presley, Fleetwood Mac and Bon Jovi — and according to some, it’s home to multiple active spirits.
entertainment.body:
In the summer of 2020, the historic Florida Theatre in Jacksonville, Fla., used the COVID-induced halt in touring to take care of some much-needed renovations. The former movie palace — which is now owned by the City of Jacksonville and the non-profit Florida Theatre Performing Arts Center — underwent capital improvements including new lighting, sound and video systems, as well as new seats — save for a pair in the balcony that were restored rather than replaced in honor of the theater’s ghostly friend, “J.”

According to multiple employees who spoke with Billboard , the grand, 1,900-seat movie palace — which took over a corner of Forsyth and Newman Streets that was formerly the site of a police station and jail — has hosted several paranormal specialists who claim to have witnessed ghostly activity in Section 500, Row E, Seat 2. This includes a figure seen sitting in the seat on video and sightings of what several have called an orb hovering over it. The alleged ghost haunting this spot got its name after a psychic consultant to a WJCT Public Television production said the apparition called himself J (either for Jay or Joy, an emotion the psychic said J felt for the theater). The psychic also noted that J was there to protect rather than harm.

“A lot of times when I’m in the theater, there’s only one seat that’s ever up, and it’s always the ghost seat,” says the theater’s marketing director Sarah Kraynik .

“There’s not a big sign [that] says ‘Ghost’ or ‘Beware of Ghost.’ It’s just, if you know, you know,” says Florida Theatre president Kevin Stone .

While the chairs look like all the others in the building, the theater gets calls from people throughout the year specifically asking to book the ghost seats, Stone says. The theater even sells a bumper sticker that reads, “I sat with the ghosts at the Florida Theatre.”

“There’s a little bit of a premium to those chairs,” says Stone. “It doesn’t hurt that the ghost seat is in the first row of the middle balcony, so there’s nobody in front of you.”

J may not be the only presence hanging around the ornate Mediterranean Revival building. Stone says construction workers have reported paint cans flying through the air and that multiple people have heard an electrical hum coming from unplugged items. Other strange occurrences, he says, include doors closing on their own and reports from theater staff of an unknown figure appearing in the projection booth.

entertainment.title: Lil Baby Is Open to ‘Stepping Out of the Box’ to Collab With Sabrina Carpenter: ‘I Could Make It Work’
entertainment.summary: A former staple of the pop ecosystem, the rapper/pop star link-up is essentially extinct.
entertainment.body:
What used to be a staple of pop music — the rapper/pop star collaboration — is basically dead. However, Lil Baby is willing to do his part to have the sector be revitalized.

Baby sat down with The New York Times’ Popcast on Thursday for an extensive conversation, which spilled into his aspirations to try stepping outside of his comfort zone for a glossy collaboration with a pop star like Sabrina Carpenter.

“I’m still in that box a little bit, but I’m more open to stepping out of the box,” he said. “The box is bigger. As I step out a little bit, the box gets bigger.

Baby continued: “Even a Sabrina Carpenter — just say, for instance, in my head, I don’t have a song on my hard drive to send to her. But if we sit there and create something, or she sends me something, I feel like I could make it work.”

Pop star/rapper collaborations have become a rarity. Camila Cabello has been attempting to keep the crossover team-ups alive. The former Fifth Harmony singer recruited Drake for “Hot Uptown” and “Uuugly,” while also joining forces with Playboi Carti for “I Luv It” (No. 81 Billboard Hot 100 peak). All three were released in 2024 and landed on her C,XOXO album, which debuted at No. 13 on the Billboard 200.

Dua Lipa enlisted DaBaby for the dynamic “Levitating” remix in 2020, which dominated commercially, reaching No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 2021.

Sabrina Carpenter does actually have a rap collab under her belt, clashing with Saweetie for “I Can’t Stop Me,” which landed on SC’s Singular Act II project in 2019.

As for Lil Baby, he doesn’t have Sabrina or any pop stars on his upcoming Fresh album , which is set to arrive on Nov. 6. Fans of the 4PF rapper can expect guest appearances from Future, Young Thug and Rylo Rodriguez.
